findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: propertycheck_catalogue, propertycheck_account · Private data: property_coverage, property_payment_options, property_report_one_off, property_report_card_checkout, property_report, propertycheck_lookup · Public sink: property_report_one_off.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: propertycheck_catalogue, propertycheck_account · Private data: property_coverage, property_payment_options, property_report_one_off, property_report_card_checkout, property_report, propertycheck_lookup · Public sink: property_report_one_off

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "propertycheck_lookup" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Flood, bushfire, transport noise, major electricity infrastructure, planning zone, land use, school catchments, nearest public transport, police division and measured traffic for one point on the Gold Coast. Costs one credit. Refused, and not charged for, outside the serviced area." → after: "API KEY REQUIRED — 1 credit. Deprecated compatibility alias retained for existing clients; prefer property_coverage followed by property_report for new integrations and retry-safe stored reports. Use only when a legacy client needs the complete PropertyCheck package returned directly for one Gold Co"

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
